title: Measure the Earth with a shadow
hook: Can a stick's shadow and one walk size the whole planet? How?

knows: that a full circle is 360 degrees
doesNotKnow: how the size of the Earth was first measured
that a shadow angle and one distance are enough

misconception: The size of the Earth could only be found after satellites or long voyages.
objective: The learner can explain that, with parallel sunlight, the shadow angle equals the angle at the Earth's centre, so circumference = (360 / angle) x distance.

claims.text: This lesson's story: at noon a well at Syene has no shadow, a pole's shadow in Alexandria makes 7.2 degrees, and the distance is 5,000 stadia, giving 250,000 stadia.
claims.source: Stage basis (Demo.tsx v5): the chip 'The story: 7.2°' sets the shadow angle to 7.2 (ACCOUNT.angle); the distance line reads 'Distance Syene to Alexandria, in the story: 5,000 stadia.' in story mode (v5, W-272; modern mode reads 'Distance Syene to Alexandria: 843 km.', c3); the circumference readout computes 360 / 7.2 x 5,000 = 250,000 stadia; the Seen line records '7.2° → 50 arcs, 250,000 stadia', which the reveal quotes. The question and the Syene label ('Syene, in the story:' / 'Sun overhead, no shadow') stipulate the no-shadow well as the lesson's setup. Reworded per W-258 ruling (company/reviews/eratosthenes-shadow/2026-10-14-fact-check.md 'Ruling on W-258'); demo-builder v4, W-260. Builder statement, not self-verified. Needs a fact-checker re-check against the stage. | FC pass 28 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-262): DISPUTED. Independent of the drafter (wording by evaluation-steward, W-258; built by demo-builder). The mismatch is on the stage: the distance line reads "Distance Syene to Alexandria: 5,000 stadia." with no story frame, in story mode on every path, including the opening state (angle 20, no chip active) and the predict phase. That is a bare factual statement about a real distance in a unit whose length is unknown (c4), the kind of sentence the W-258 ruling says must be stage-only. Fix (demo-builder): in story mode the line reads "Distance Syene to Alexandria, in the story: 5,000 stadia." (modern mode unchanged; covered by c3). Re-check after the fix. | demo-builder v5 (2026-10-14, W-272): story-mode distance line changed to the FC pass 28 wording, verbatim. claims.text: Because the Sun is so far away its rays arrive parallel, so the shadow angle equals the angle at the Earth's centre between the two places.
claims.source: Alternate angles between parallel lines (the rays) cut by a transversal (the radius through Alexandria). The Sun's rays across Earth's diameter diverge by under 0.01 degrees (12,742 km / 150 million km), which is negligible here.

claims.text: With modern numbers, 7.11 degrees and 843 km give 50.6 arcs and 42,684 km, within 7% of the true 40,008 km.
claims.source: Latitudes Alexandria 31.20 N 29.92 E and Aswan 24.09 N 32.90 E (gazetteer, from memory, not checked online); difference 7.11 degrees; great-circle distance 843.2 km by geoDistance with R = 6,371.0088 km, computed in Demo.tsx; 843 x 360 / 7.11 = 42,684 km, which the stage's Seen line and the reveal both show as 42,684 km (the circumference readout's rounding); 360 / 7.11 = 50.6 at the arcs readout's one decimal. 40,008 km is the WGS84 meridional circumference (about 40,007.86 km, from memory). The cities are not on one meridian (3 degrees of longitude apart), which accounts for much of the excess. | FC pass 26 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Coordinates checked against GeoNames (npm cities.json, GeoNames gazetteer extract, opened locally): Alexandria 31.20176 N 29.91582 E, Aswan 24.09082 N 32.89942 E, which round to the lesson's 31.20/29.92 and 24.09/32.90. 40,008 km: GeographicLib (npm geographiclib-geodesic) WGS84 a = 6378137 m, f = 1/298.257223563, 4 x geodesic(0,0 -> 90,0) = 40,007.86 km. Own node with d3-geo geoDistance and R = 6,371.0088: 7.11 degrees, 843.2 km (843), 360/7.11 = 50.6, 843 x 360/7.11 = 42,684 km, 6.7% over (prints 7%). With unrounded GeoNames coordinates the circumference is 42,700 km, still within 7%. | 2026-10-14 (v6, demo-builder): reveal sentence unchanged; the Arcs round the circle and Circumference readouts moved from a readout row into the picture beside the circle (same arcsText / fmt rounding; the unit is on the line under the number). Status left as is.

claims.text: Nobody knows a stadion's exact length, so how close Eratosthenes was in km cannot be said.
claims.source: Proposed stadion lengths range from about 157 m to about 185 m (e.g. Engels 1985, 'The Length of Eratosthenes' Stade', American Journal of Philology; from memory, not checked online). | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v6, build 6 phone fit, demo-builder): reveal sentence reworded to 'Nobody knows a stadion's exact length, so we cannot say how close Eratosthenes was in km.' (was 'the exact length of a stadion'); meaning intended unchanged; needs a fresh check. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 34 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-363): VERIFIED. Independent of the drafter. Rendered reveal (Playwright, 390x844, QA path): 'Nobody knows a stadion's exact length, so we cannot say how close Eratosthenes was in km.', same meaning as the claim. Source: the stadion Eratosthenes used is disputed in the literature: Hultsch 1882 ~157.5 m; Firsov 1972 ~157.7 m (from 81 Eratosthenes/Strabo distances); Engels, 'The Length of Eratosthenes' Stade', American Journal of Philology 106(3): 298-311 (1985), doi 10.2307/295030; Dicks 1960 and Rawlins 1982 treat 185 m (Attic) as settled; Lelgemann 2004 ~158.7 m; Revue d'histoire des sciences 1/2024 argues ~158 m. These bibliographic details agree across independent web-search results; full texts could not be opened (WebFetch DNS failure for every host this session), so this rests on attested published disagreement, not on a read article. Node: 250,000 stadia x 157.5 m = 39,375 km (-1.6% vs 40,008) and x 185 m = 46,250 km (+15.6%), so the km error does depend on the unknown length and 'cannot say' follows. Recommend opening Engels 1985 when any checker can.

claims.text: This lesson's story: at noon the Sun stands straight overhead at Syene, so the well there has no shadow.
claims.source: A vertical well shows no shadow on its sides only when the Sun is at the zenith (rays parallel to the well's axis), so 'no shadow' in the story and 'Sun straight overhead' are the same stipulation. Stage label (two lines): 'Syene, in the story:' / 'Sun overhead, no shadow'; the reveal says the claim word for word. The lesson stipulates this as its own setup and makes no claim about what any ancient source reports or that the Sun was exactly overhead at the real Syene (24.09 N, north of the Tropic). Reworded per W-258 ruling (company/reviews/eratosthenes-shadow/2026-10-14-fact-check.md 'Ruling on W-258'); demo-builder v4, W-260. Builder statement, not self-verified. Needs a fact-checker re-check against the stage. | FC pass 28 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-262): VERIFIED. Independent of the drafter (wording by evaluation-steward, W-258). Stage v4 checked on every path: the reveal sentence is the claim word for word; the Syene label reads "Syene, in the story:" / "Sun overhead, no shadow" in both modes and in predict; the stage draws the vertical ray straight down to Syene with no shadow line there; the question frames noon and the well as "this lesson's story". Derivation re-run in node: a vertical stick's shadow is h x tan(z), which is zero only at z = 0 (0.0087 h at 0.5 degrees, 0.126 h at 7.2), so "no shadow" and "Sun overhead" are one stipulation. No sentence asserts what a historical source says or that the real Syene had an overhead Sun. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v6, build 6 phone fit, demo-builder): the reveal sentence 'This lesson's story: at noon the Sun stands straight overhead at Syene, so the well there has no shadow.' is cut; the claim now rests on the stage label 'Syene, in the story: / Sun overhead, no shadow' (svg text, unchanged words) and the predict question ('In this lesson's story, at noon a well in Syene has no shadow'). Needs a fresh check that the stage alone carries it. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 34 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-363): VERIFIED. Independent of the drafter. With the reveal sentence cut, the claim rests on the stage: rendered (Playwright, 390x844) on predict (locked), the opening state (20.00 deg), story mode, modern mode and with the reveal open, the svg labels 'Syene, in the story:' / 'Sun overhead, no shadow' are present in every state and both modes, and the predict question reads 'In this lesson's story, at noon a well in Syene has no shadow'. The vertical ray meets Syene with no shadow drawn. Together they say the claim: noon (question), Sun overhead and no shadow (label), framed as the story's (both). Derivation unchanged: a vertical stick's shadow is h tan z, zero only at z = 0. Non-blocking: at 390 px the Syene label overlaps a dashed sunlight ray ('in| the story'); legible.

claims.text: Hook: a stick's shadow and one walked distance are enough to size the whole planet.
claims.source: Hook v4: 'Can a stick's shadow and one walk size the whole planet? How?' (was 'Over 2,000 years ago someone sized the whole planet with a stick and a walk. How?', an unrecorded historical claim; reworded stage-only per W-258 ruling, W-260). With parallel rays the shadow angle equals the centre angle (c2), so circumference = (360 / angle) x distance; the stage computes it from the shadow angle and the distance line alone. The hook names no number, so it does not point to an option. Builder statement, not self-verified. | FC pass 28 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14, W-262): VERIFIED. Independent of the drafter (hook reworded by demo-builder per W-258, W-260). The hook is a question and names no source, date or person. It does not point to an option (none of 7/50/360 appears). On the stage the circumference is computed from the shadow angle and the distance alone (circ = 360/angle x d.dist; node: 7.2 and 5,000 give 250,000; 7.11 and 843 give 42,684). The conditions the claim rests on are all supplied by the stage: parallel rays (c2), the stipulated no-shadow well as the zero reference (c5), and the two places on one north-south line (the cross-section; the modern cities are 3 degrees of longitude apart, covered by c3). The reveal sentence "The method needed only a shadow and a distance." makes the same claim and is covered here. Nit for the builder, not blocking: neither the question nor the reveal says the two places lie north-south; the recall question does.

recall.question: Two towns 1,000 km apart lie on one north-south line. At the same noon their shadows differ by 9 degrees. How big is the planet round?
recall.why: The shadow difference is the angle at the centre. 9 degrees is 1/40 of 360, so the circumference is 40 x 1,000 km = 40,000 km.
